newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Sofia approves joint co to build Balkan oil route.
newsitem.headline: Sofia approves joint co to build Balkan oil route.

text.p: Bulgaria's cabinet has approved a proposal for the establishment of a joint venture with Russia and Greece to build and operate an oil pipeline.
A joint venture, named Transbalkanneft, will build the pipeline to supply Russian crude to the Balkans, if Russia and Greece agree, Construction Minister Doncho Konakchiev said.

Bulgaria, Russia and Greece plan a tanker route from the Russian Black Sea port of Novorossiisk to Bourgas in Bulgaria, from where a pipeline will carry the Russian crude to Alexandroupolis in Greece.
The project is expected to cost some $700-$800 million.
Konakchiev said Russia would have a 50 percent stake, while Bulgaria and Greece will have 25 percent each.
A tripartite meeting at a government level is expected to be held in February.

In a separate development, the Albanian, Macedonian and Bulgarian Oil Corporation (AMBO) said on Friday the feasibility study for AMBO's Trans-Balkan Oil Pipeline, conducted by the international engineering company Brown & Root Ltd in London, has determined that this pipeline is economically viable.
"The feasibility study clearly demonstrates that this pipeline will be both economically competitve and complimentary with other proposed pipelines," the statement said.

The 567-mile (907 km) pipeline will carry oil from Russia, Kazakhstan and Azerbaijan from Bulgaria's port of Bourgas to the Albanian port of Vlore on the Adriatic, bypassing Turkey's congested Bosphorus Straits leading from the Black Sea.
The 36 inch (91 cm) pipeline will have a daily capacity of 750,000 barrels and is expected to cost $825 million.
